program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. You receive no reference label or optimization feedback. Return status, evidence, reported confidence (0..1 or null), and used_dependency_ids naming every supplied context check_id exactly once in saved order.
Supports receive source and edited images. Answer only the saved proposition using its binding and criteria. Use pass/fail/unknown. Context is advisory unless listed in required_dependencies. A negative context observation is usable evidence. Unknown, skipped, or invalid context is not a failure and must not stop an independent image inspection. Inspect the images yourself; do not repeat a parent's answer. Return unknown when the relevant fact cannot be established. Confidence reports confidence in this answer, not calibrated correctness.
Fulfillment receives NO images. Use only saved support evidence, original instruction/rubric and frozen composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Supporting passes answer specific propositions, not a count of completed edits. Their polarity can differ. Apply saved alternatives: optional uncertainty need not prevent a known outcome, but a required unresolved fact makes that outcome unresolved. Never invent a visual fact or convert missing evidence into failure. A conditional skip is not non-applicability. All applicable requested outcomes complete gives yes; no requested progress gives no; known progress short of completion gives partial. Unrelated changes are not progress.

fulfillment: The node’s outcome logic is appropriately conservative, but its evidence binding is too brittle: it treats the edited objects as unidentifiable rather than assessing whether the blue printed item could be the source paper and whether the reddish object could be the cup. Improve the supporting checks to compare source and edited objects using visible shape, material, color, and scene context while allowing appearance changes; separately assess completion (paper visibly inside the cup) and partial progress (a plausible attempt to insert the same paper into the same cup). Here, the edit shows a hand holding a blue printed item against or near a reddish rounded object, with no clear evidence that the paper is inside a cup or that either object matches the source. That supports no progress only if the checks can establish the objects and rule out relevant progress; otherwise retain unknown. Do not convert high confidence in unresolved identity into negative evidence. Keep the existing distinction between complete, partial, no progress, and unresolved, and investigate whether the checks’ identity-matching criterion is causing valid visual evidence to be discarded. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
s2: The binding is too restrictive when it requires confidently identifying the exact source objects before evaluating progress. Make the supporting check compare plausible object correspondence using visible shape, material, color, and scene context while allowing substantial appearance changes; then assess the action relation separately. In these images, the edited blue printed item may be the paper and the reddish rounded object may be the cup, but neither match nor insertion is clear. Do not treat high-confidence uncertainty as evidence of no progress: return unknown unless the objects can be matched and relevant progress ruled out. Preserve the distinction between completion, partial progress, no progress, and unresolved; no transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
s1: The binding and criteria are overly strict about matching the exact source objects, so the check returns unknown instead of evaluating visible evidence. Compare plausible correspondence using shape, material, color, and scene context while allowing appearance changes; then assess object identity and the action relation separately. Here, the source has a white sheet and blue cup, while the edit shows a hand holding a blue printed sheet against a reddish rounded object. The sheet could be the paper, but the object is not clearly identifiable as the cup and the paper is not visibly inside it. Do not infer no progress from uncertain identity, or treat high confidence in uncertainty as negative evidence. Preserve the distinction between complete, partial, no progress, and unresolved; return no only when the relevant objects can be matched and the image rules out progress, otherwise retain unknown. The reference label constrains the aggregate, not the atomic check. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
